plan.contextChunk: This figure is a single plot tracing the flight path of a batted ball across a distance-versus-height grid. The horizontal axis is labeled "Distance (ft)" and runs from 0 to 600 with ticks every 100 feet; the vertical axis is labeled "Height (ft)" and carries labeled ticks at 100, 200, and 300, with faint dotted gridlines filling the plotting area. A teal curve leaves the origin, climbs as a broad downward-opening parabola to a maximum slightly above 150 feet near a distance of about 290 feet, then falls back to the horizontal axis a little past 560 feet, with small arrowheads spaced along its length showing the direction of travel. A leader line labeled "Position of hitter" points to the curve's start at the origin, and a second leader labeled "Trajectory of ball" points to a small circular marker on the rising branch near 200 feet. A short red rectangle stands on the horizontal axis at 400 feet and is labeled "Outfield wall"; the curve passes far above its top. Setting the wall directly beneath the arc invites the reader to compare the ball's height at that distance against the height of the barrier. The plot renders a projectile path in a form that settles whether the hit clears the wall.

interactionPlan.concept: A projectile clears an outfield wall when the trajectory height at the wall's horizontal distance is greater than the wall's height.
elements: horizontal axis labeled 'Distance (ft)' spanning 0 to 600 with labeled ticks at 0, 100, 200, 300, 400, 500, and 600
vertical axis labeled 'Height (ft)' spanning 0 to 300 with labeled ticks at 100, 200, and 300
faint dotted rectangular gridlines across the plotting area
teal downward-opening parabolic trajectory curve starting at the hitter near (0,0), reaching a maximum a little above 150 ft near 290 ft, and landing a little past 560 ft
small teal arrowheads along the trajectory indicating the ball's direction of travel
label 'Position of hitter' with leader line pointing to the origin
label 'Trajectory of ball' with leader line pointing to the rising branch of the curve near 200 ft
movable circular marker on the trajectory showing the ball's selected distance from the hitter
vertical guide line from the selected trajectory marker down to the horizontal axis
height readout showing the ball's height at the selected distance
short red outfield wall rectangle standing on the horizontal axis
label 'Outfield wall' near the red wall
comparison highlight at the wall position showing the ball height versus the fixed wall height
clearance status label reading either 'Clears wall' or 'Does not clear wall'
optional sampled distance-height points lying on the same parabolic path when sample mode is enabled

interactions.label: Distance from hitter
interactions.teaches: The graph represents a height value for every horizontal distance, so dragging along the path makes the height-at-distance relationship concrete.

interactions.label: Outfield wall position
interactions.teaches: Whether the hit is a home run is decided by comparing the ball's height and the wall's height at the same horizontal distance.

interactions.label: View
interactions.teaches: The smooth projectile curve and a table-like set of plotted distance-height samples describe the same motion in two representations.

demo_steps.title: Read the trajectory as height over distance
demo_steps.narration: The ball starts at the hitter, rises along a parabolic arc, then returns to the ground. Move the distance marker to see that each horizontal distance corresponds to one ball height.

demo_steps.title: Compare the ball with the wall
demo_steps.narration: At the wall's distance, the important question is not where the ball eventually lands, but whether the curve is above the top of the wall at that exact x-value.

demo_steps.title: Move the wall
demo_steps.narration: Slide the wall left and right to test different fence distances. The verdict changes only when the wall is placed where the ball's trajectory is lower than the wall height.

demo_steps.title: See the same motion as data points
demo_steps.narration: Switching to sampled points shows the same arc as individual distance-height measurements on the grid, linking the graph to numerical table values.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: Clearing the wall is a vertical comparison at one horizontal distance: ball height at the wall's x-value versus wall height.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Use a clean 2D coordinate grid with black axes and light dotted gridlines. Draw the trajectory as a thick teal downward-opening parabola with arrowheads along the direction of flight. The curve should begin at the origin, peak slightly above 150 ft around 290 ft, and hit the ground a little past 560 ft. Place the red wall initially at 400 ft on the x-axis as a short vertical rectangle, far below the curve. The movable ball marker should sit directly on the trajectory with a vertical guide to the x-axis and a nearby numeric height readout. In sampled-points mode, replace or de-emphasize the continuous curve with evenly spaced teal points that still clearly trace the same parabolic arc.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Slider for distance from the hitter: the learner drags a marker along the trajectory, the height readout and vertical drop to the x-axis update, and the parabola's height-at-distance relationship becomes concrete.
- Slider for outfield wall position: the learner moves the wall left or right, the figure highlights whether the ball is above or below the wall at that distance, and clearing the wall becomes a comparison of two heights at one x-value.
- Toggle between path and sampled points: the learner switches from the smooth trajectory to discrete distance-height samples, the same arc appears as points on the grid, and the connection between graph, table values, and projectile motion becomes clear.

authoredContext:
The ball is 141.8 feet in the air when it soars out of the ballpark. It was indeed a home run. See the figure.

Plotted trajectory of a hit ball, showing the position of the batter at the origin, the ball's path in the shape of a wide downward facing parabola, and the outfield wall as a vertical line segment rising to 10 ft under the ball's path.

discrepancies: The generated default view adds a dashed vertical guide at x = 200 and a numeric height label "141 ft" that are not present in the source figure.
A green vertical comparison bracket and "Clears wall" label are added at the outfield wall; the source only shows a short red wall marker with no clearance annotation.
The grid in the generated plot appears as solid gray lines rather than the fine dotted gridlines in the source.
The x-axis tick labels are rotated diagonally in the generated figure, while the source uses horizontal tick labels.
The outfield wall is drawn taller and more visually emphasized than the small red wall marker in the source.
evaluation.notes: The main projectile trajectory, axes, wall, and labels are recognizable and conceptually accurate, but the default view includes several extra teaching annotations that make it less faithful as a drop-in replacement.
action_items: Remove or hide the dashed distance guide, height readout, green clearance bracket, and "Clears wall" label in the default state; reserve them for an interactive step if desired.
Change the grid styling to fine dotted lines to better match the textbook figure.
Force horizontal x-axis tick labels and adjust padding so the axis labels resemble the source more closely.
Reduce the outfield wall marker height and visual emphasis to match the short red marker in the reference.
